summary: Documented a mechanism the account had been using implicitly: how the module enforces the ordering and completion duties it places on the application. Source reading shows fatal guards rather than clamps — appending entries whose predecessor is below the commit index panics (log.go 136-140), committing past the last index panics (322-328), reporting an applied index outside [previously applied, committed] panics (330-341), accepting application past committed panics (344-356), and a non-positive application-size budget panics (234-238) — while the only tolerated adjustments are non-fatal: the outstanding-size counter saturates at zero and application pauses until the client acknowledges progress. Rewriting entries above the commit index is deliberately allowed, which is how a follower truncates a divergent uncommitted tail. Recorded as a Fact with five cited ranges, a child question and an interpretation (conclusion explained, defect_claim null), noting the two consequences that matter for reading this run's evidence: the before/after counters could not have been silently clamped, and a misreporting client brings down its own process rather than corrupting the state machine — with the honest caveat that one guard can also fire on a value the module computes itself, and that no guard was triggered in this run. Validation passed with no execution requested.
